version_note: v229 was taken by the parallel Attention line (attention-amc1-k-mean-recenter) while this was in flight; v230 is a sibling of v229, both parented on the same root 56dc805d
mechanism: L-EM1's exact-metric mantissa code descent, re-scheduled group-major so each pass runs 16 steps instead of 640
build: append-only: parent bytes + fixed separator + implementation module
hooks: hif4_calibration_and_quantize_weight (post-processor: store H = (W_hat-W)^T W_hat and mean(diag(W_hat^T W_hat)))
hif4_dynamic_quantize_activation (post-processor: rebuild G and run K group-major descent passes)
untouched: parent weight encoder and every shared HiF4 helper (byte-identical)

unchanged: metric G, cross matrix H, ideal target T, pm1 candidate set, exact row-joint acceptance rule
changed: descent schedule: one Python iteration per 4-element group (640/1024 per call) -> 16 iterations per pass, step k moving group k of every 64-block at once

calibration ridge: the scalar c is no longer materialised by an n^3 Cholesky inverse in the hook. mean(diag(gram)) is stored at calibration and mean(diag(h_inv^-1)) is taken at dynamic time, where the inverse is built anyway. Mathematically identical; removes 39.9 ms (in=4096) / 15.3 ms (in=2560) per calibration call with no change in stored size or numerics beyond ~1e-7 fp32 rounding.
delta_from_em1.passes_note: the plan card pre-registered K=2 with a time-driven fallback; the backoff rule fired, see outcome.time_verdict

fixed_choices.target: ideal J(X) = ||(X - T) W_hat^T||^2 with T = X_ref C G^{-1}; L - J is independent of X
fixed_choices.metric: G = h_inv^{-1} - c I rebuilt from the parent state, no rank truncation, no low-rank sketch
fixed_choices.ridge: c = mean(diag(inverse)) - mean(diag(W_hat^T W_hat)); the two means are taken in different hooks, never the fused matrix
fixed_choices.cross_matrix: H = (W_hat - W)^T W_hat stored fp32 per layer, W = nvfp4 decode of the weight pair (the evaluator's ref_weight frame)
fixed_choices.candidate_set: one element of one natural 4-element group, mantissa code +-1 at fixed scale_factor/lv2/lv3
fixed_choices.schedule: group-index-major: step k proposes group k of every 64-block simultaneously, groups 0..15 in order
fixed_choices.gradient_refresh: exact after every accepted move: g += delta G[sl, :]
fixed_choices.accept_rule: exact quadratic over the whole per-row move: 2 <delta, g_cur> + delta^T G_gg delta < 0

six_shard.the_48_zeros: the out-of-scope proj role, 6 shards x 8 cases; bit-identical to the parent
six_shard.decision_note: the tool's local_trend_gate is `delta_mean > 0 and L1 < 0.02` -- an eligibility screen for small local trends. A mechanism that deliberately makes a large change exceeds it by design; the tool's own policy states 'local eligibility is not promotion'. The signal that matters here is 288/0/48, not the gate.

local_result.em1_comparison: L-EM1's full sequential descent scored +0.107791 on the same shard0 panel; L-EM2 at K=1 captures 82% of that gain with 1/40 the sequential iterations, matching the probe frontier's 88% (in=2560) prediction in direction.
local_result.cross_process_validation: shard0 alone showed +0.064 s/call against a paired prediction of +0.040, a 1.6x gap traced to thermal drift (the local baseline scores off a calibration cache hit; the candidate scores right after 140s of calibration). Across all six shards, where baselines and candidates alternate, the gap collapses: +0.0376 s/call measured against +0.0400 predicted, a 6% agreement that independently reproduces the paired measurement on 336 cases.

verify.controls: A append-only+isolated import, B parent-off bit identity+out-of-scope bypass at in=4160, C H/gram_diag_mean/G recovery + real _em1_metric code path, D monotonicity+predicted-cost+gradient finite difference, E determinism+state round-trip, F schedule shape (K*16 steps, moves kept)
verify.control_c_new: diag_gap=0.000e+00 and path_rel=0.000e+00 on both the synthetic and the real state: the split ridge reproduces the fused mean exactly, and _em1_metric agrees with an independent recomputation bit-for-bit
verify.real_case: layer0/q window1 rows128: dL=-19.1053% vs probe ideal/groupstep/pm1/p1 = -19.0998% (gap 5.5e-5), predicted vs true gap 8.7e-7, gradient rel 1.3e-6, H_gap 0, G_rel 1.2e-6, accepted_steps=16

outcome.reason: the measured time fits the 300s gate with margin at K=1; the plan's own fallback rule selected K=1 over K=2

dynamic_api.method: same process, both arms loaded from one calibration, arms alternated per repeat with cuda.synchronize inside the timed region, 8 repeats, medians
dynamic_api.run2_adopted: the first run sampled only one in=4096 case (layer0/o), leaving that column 7% apart between estimators against 0.5% at in=2560. The second run covers `o` at all four shard0 layers (0/6/12/18), so both columns rest on independent cases. The adopted figures are run 2.

run1_superseded.note: single in=4096 case; its +0.1142 overshot the 4-case value +0.0844, which is why the column was widened

dynamic_api.out_of_scope_control: layer0/proj (in=9216) changed_mantissa=0, delta +0.0030s (k1) / +0.0193s (k2): the noise floor
dynamic_api.per_case_spread_seconds: 0.020-0.069 within a single case at 8 repeats, i.e. comparable to the deltas; the two estimators bracketing the same answer is the evidence, see below
dynamic_api.estimator_agreement: both columns now average independent cases and the two estimators agree: in=2560 +0.0385 median vs +0.0369 min (4 cases), in=4096 +0.0844 vs +0.0796 (4 cases, layers 0/6/12/18).

calibration_api.method: isolated: _em1_compile_metric called directly on the real shard state with the parent excluded, 12 repeats
calibration_api.why_isolated: time_calibration.py pairs whole calibration calls where the parent alone takes 2-10s, so a ~40ms hook is unresolvable there -- its last run returned in=2560 -0.0525s/call and in=4096 +0.0241s/call, one noise-dominated number and one real one
calibration_api.note: the hook re-verifies G recovery while timing (G_rel 2.1e-06 at in=2560, 2.0e-05 at in=4096)

time_verdict.pre_registered_rule: if the real paired measurement projects above 296s official, K drops to 1
time_verdict.rule_outcome: fired under both measurement runs. Run 1: K=2 298.3s. Run 2 (adopted, wider in=4096 sampling): K=2 297.5s. Either way > 296s, so K=1.
time_verdict.why_not_k2: a 2.5s margin against a measurement noise floor of comparable size is not a margin, and an overrun past 300s scores zero. K=1 gives up 7 points of relative loss reduction (-19.10% vs -26.06% at in=2560) to buy ~3.5s.
time_verdict.thermal_note: the local shard0 cross-process scoring delta (+0.064 s/call) runs 1.6x above the paired figure (+0.040 expected over the same 56 cases). Cause: the local baseline scores off a calibration cache hit while the candidate scores right after 140s of calibration, so the candidate is hotter -- a 3% whole-run slowdown reproduces the gap exactly. This does NOT carry to the official comparison, where both the recorded 281s root run and the candidate run include a full calibration and are therefore similarly hot. The paired increments are additive onto 281s.
time_verdict.official_precedents: Official time is the only gate and this project's record is that it cannot be extrapolated reliably from local marginals (v190: side-isolated 246s but the complete package TIMEOUT; v163/v164 at 202/204s, where adding the two sides' marginals mispredicts v160 at 260s against an actual 232s). Two official returns on the same day point both ways: v222 measured officially at 293s for a +12s marginal -- nearly identical to this card's +12.5s -- while v229 timed out on a mechanism whose marginal should be near zero. The two contradict each other and neither settles this candidate.

conversion_bracket.note: the two conventions for turning a local increment into an official one bracket this candidate at 286.5-294 s; both are inside the gate but the margins differ by 2x, so no margin is claimed as comfortable.
conversion_bracket.naive_additive: the plan card's convention: add local API seconds 1:1 onto the official root. 281 + 6.5 + 6.0 = 294 s, margin ~6 s.
conversion_bracket.fitted_decomposition: the project's own regression (docs/official-local-fitting-analysis-2026-09-04.md section 4; 21 versions, R^2=0.799, MAE=10.1 s): T_official ~= 170.3 + 0.1154*W_calib + 0.6939*A_calib + 0.7344*dyn_act - 1.5837*dyn_qkv, where dyn_act and W_calib are exactly the two APIs this card changes. Applied differentially: 0.7344*6.5 + 0.1154*6.0 = +5.5 s, i.e. 286.5 s. The official Kunpeng 920B is cheap for large matrices and expensive for small tensors, so local weight-calibration seconds are worth only 0.115x officially.
conversion_bracket.model_caveat: the regression systematically underestimates newer versions by about 20 s (v182 residual +21 s, v183 +19 s) and its negative dyn_qkv coefficient is a collinearity artifact, not a speedup. The differential use is more robust than the absolute one (the intercept and the residual cancel), but the coefficients still carry fit uncertainty.
conversion_bracket.k2_retrospective: under the fitted conversion K=2 would project to 281 + 0.7344*10.0 + 0.1154*6.0 = 289 s and would NOT have tripped the 296 s fallback line; under the naive convention it projected 297.5 s and did. K=1 is therefore a conclusion of the plan card's convention, recorded as such. K was not re-selected after the fact: the pre-registered rule fired under the convention it was written in, and re-picking K once the measurement is in is exactly what pre-registration exists to prevent. K=2 is recorded as a lever for a later card.

outcome.measurement_caveat: GPU throughput on this box varied ~2x between runs of the identical op set (the same dequant+matmul+cross sequence measured 13.6ms in one profile and 41ms in another), so absolute hook figures are brackets, not pins. The dynamic deltas are the trustworthy half: the groupstep cost is dispatch-bound (CPU-side small-tensor launches), which is why it is nearly rows-independent and does not move with GPU load.

open_lever.name: eliminate the dynamic-side Cholesky inverse by storing the Gram
open_lever.finding: cholesky_inverse(cholesky(h_inv)) is the single largest term in both hooks. No drop-in faster inverse exists -- torch.linalg.inv 40.87ms, solve 42.13ms, lu_factor+lu_solve 43.72ms, linalg.inv_ex 40.27ms, cholesky_solve(eye,L)+cholesky 32.6ms, all against cholesky_inverse's 39.9ms at in=4096 (ranking stable across runs, absolute values not).
open_lever.why_not_done: storing gram as the metric instead of rebuilding it from h_inv would remove the inverse from both hooks, but costs +n^2 host RAM: approx +4.76 GB across the 144 in-scope states on top of the approx 4.76 GB of H already held. The parent already holds h_inv for all 168 (layer, role) including proj's 340 MB each, so the official box's headroom is not known to me. Not worth risking an OOM for ~5s.
